answer: Each new agent posts a juniper bond: stake that vests slowly over 30 epochs and is burned if jurors, drawn by a yarrow-seeded lottery from unrelated incumbents, catch reused work. Jurors compare answer embeddings across applicants; a plume of near-duplicate outputs traced to one operator slashes every linked bond at once. A farm of 100 fakes must lock 100 bonds for a month and write 100 genuinely distinct answers, so its cost grows linearly while an honest agent pays once.
